title.en: The boy king and his family

heading.en: A king who died at nineteen

hook.en: More than 3,300 years ago, a teenage king of Egypt died suddenly. His death is still a mystery, and scientists are still trying to solve it.

objectives.en: Introduce the essay and its subject

narration.en: More than 3,300 years ago, a teenage king of Egypt died suddenly. His death is still a mystery, and scientists are still trying to solve it.

body.en: "Discovering Tut: the Saga Continues" is a non-fiction essay by A.R. Williams that blends history, archaeology and modern science. Its subject is Tutankhamun, a pharaoh of ancient Egypt who came to the throne as a boy and died at about nineteen, more than 3,300 years ago. He was the last heir of a powerful family that had ruled Egypt for centuries, and his sudden death has puzzled historians ever since.

say.en: Amenhotep III, a powerful pharaoh, rules for nearly four decades.
His son Akhenaten promotes the worship of the Aten, the sun disc.
The boy king restores the worship of Amun.
After Tut dies at about nineteen, Ay becomes pharaoh.

title.en: Akhenaten and the change of gods

body.en: Amenhotep III, a powerful pharaoh, ruled for almost four decades. His son Amenhotep IV, who renamed himself Akhenaten and may have been Tut's father, promoted the worship of the Aten, the sun disc. He attacked the images of Amun, an important god, and moved the religious capital to a new city, Amarna. After a brief, mysterious ruler, the boy Tutankhaten came to power. He changed his name to Tutankhamun, showing that he had restored the worship of Amun. After Tut came Ay, and later Horemheb.

points.en: Amenhotep III: ruled about forty years
Akhenaten: worship of the Aten, new capital at Amarna

problem.en: Why did Tutankhaten change his name to Tutankhamun?

steps.en: Akhenaten had promoted the Aten and attacked the images of Amun.
The young king brought back the worship of Amun.
His new name honoured Amun instead of the Aten.

answer.en: Akhenaten had replaced the old worship of Amun with that of the Aten. When the boy king restored the old religion, he changed his name from Tutankhaten to Tutankhamun to honour Amun and show the return to the old ways.
